title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Gothenburg: find the fast route
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra race from both start and goal on real-like street graphs, meeting in the middle for speed. This visualization shows how two synchronized Dijkstra searches reduce explored nodes compared to a single-source run.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ **Bidirectional Dijkstra** is like sending two teams of pathfinders—one from home and one from the destination—until they shake hands mid-route. 

🧠 **How it works (technical):** We run Dijkstra from the **start** (forward) and from the **goal** (backward) using weighted edges, maintaining frontiers with priority queues. The moment the searches meet, we can reconstruct the shortest path by combining distances from both directions—often exploring **far fewer nodes** than classic single-direction Dijkstra, especially on large graphs. 

🗺️ **Graph theory on street maps:** Think of Masthugget’s roads as a **weighted graph** where intersections are nodes and road segments are edges (with costs like time, distance, or speed). Because the graph is sparse and locally structured, bidirectional search exploits symmetry to shrink the search space without sacrificing optimality.

Bidirectional Dijkstra visualization on real-world style street graphs! 🗺️🚦

In this YouTube Shorts video, we run **Bidirectional Dijkstra** from both start and goal using priority queues, combining forward/backward distances when the frontiers meet. Learn how **graph search** works on weighted road networks (nodes = intersections, edges = road segments) and why bidirectional exploration often reduces visited nodes compared to classic Dijkstra.
